chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abu Ayyub who said: Abu Basir narrated to me who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions one day: 'Do you see if you gathered what you have of clothes and vessels, then placed some upon others, do you think it would reach the sky?' They said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah.'

He said: 'One of you should say, when he finishes his prayer: Subhanallah wal-hamdu lillah wa la ilaha illallah wallahu akbar (Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest) thirty times. And these will repel destruction, drowning, burning, falling into a well, being eaten by wild beasts, and bad death, and the calamity that descends upon the servant on that day.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting the Tashbihat thirty times after prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s teaching that the thirty post-prayer recitations of the Tashbihat act as a comprehensive spiritual shield against both physical perils—such as drowning, fire, and animal attacks—and spiritual afflictions like premature death. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the protective power of dhikr, linking the consistency of daily worship to divine preservation from the 'calamity of the day' (al-baliyya).
